```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
setwd("~/~grad school/research/8 psych sci replication/pilot")

d=read.csv("pilotdata_all.csv")
d[] <- lapply(d, function(x) {
    if(is.factor(x)) as.numeric(as.character(x)) else x
})

```

First, I want to only include topics in the main replication study if they are viewed as controversial by 1. everyone, 2. just Democrats, 3. just Republicans and 4. just Independents. Therefore, I obtained 4 corresponding means for each topic and only included topics that had means above 4 for each mean. 

```{r}
Ds=d[which(d$PA==1),]
Rs=d[which(d$PA==2),]
Is=d[which(d$PA==3),]

overallmeans=c()
Dmeans=c()
Rmeans=c()
Imeans=c()
for (x in 9:30){
  Mean= colMeans(d[x],na.rm = TRUE)
  overallmeans=c(overallmeans,Mean)
  Mean= colMeans(Ds[x],na.rm = TRUE)
  Dmeans=c(Dmeans,Mean)
  Mean= colMeans(Rs[x],na.rm = TRUE)
  Rmeans=c(Rmeans,Mean)
  Mean= colMeans(Is[x],na.rm = TRUE)
  Imeans=c(Imeans,Mean)
}
```
These are the overall means:  
`r overallmeans`  
They are all above the midpoint of 4.   

These are the means for Democrats only:  
`r Dmeans`  
They are all above the midpoint of 4.  

These are the means for Republicans only:  
`r Rmeans`  
They are all above the midpoint of 4.  

These are the means for Independents only:  
`r Imeans`  
Q6_4 (government helping those in need) is below 4 and Q6_12 (Muslim religious rights) is below 4. Therefore, these two scales will be dropped and not included in the replication study.   

--  

For the second step, I want to confirm that the order of attitudes (from conservative to liberal) in the topic scales is validated by the pilot participants. For each scale, I will see what percentage of participants ranked the items in their intended order. Scales that were ranked in that order at least 50% of the time will be included in the replication study (given they meet the second criteria, i.e., are perceived as controversial topics). I only looked at topics that were viewed as controversial in step 1 above.
